The '''2022 Enfield London Borough Council election''' took place on 5 May 2022, alongside [[2022 London local elections|local elections in the other London boroughs]] and [[2022 United Kingdom local elections|elections to local authorities across the United Kingdom]]. All 63 members of [[Enfield London Borough Council]] were elected.

In the [[2018 Enfield London Borough Council election|previous election in 2018]], the [[Labour Party (UK)|Labour Party]] maintained its control of the council, winning 46 out of the 63 seats with the [[Conservative Party (UK)|Conservative Party]] forming the council opposition with the remaining 17 seats. The 2022 election took place under new election boundaries, which however kept the same number of councillors as before. In 2022, Labour was re-elected for a fourth term. This was the first time that Labour was re-elected with a reduced number of seats ever since the London Boroughs were created in 1964.

== Background ==

=== History ===
[[File:Enfield London UK local election 2018 map.svg|thumb|Result of the 2018 borough election]]
The thirty-two [[London boroughs]] were established in 1965 by the [[London Government Act 1963]]. They are the principal authorities in Greater London and have responsibilities including education, housing, planning, highways, social services, libraries, recreation, waste, environmental health and revenue collection. Some of the powers are shared with the [[Greater London Authority]], which also manages passenger transport, police and fire.<ref>{{Cite web|title=The essential guide to London local government {{!}} London Councils|url=https://www.londoncouncils.gov.uk/who-runs-london/essential-guide-london-local-government|access-date=2021-10-10|website=www.londoncouncils.gov.uk}}</ref>

Since its formation, Enfield has been under [[Labour Party (UK)|Labour]] or [[Conservative Party (UK)|Conservative]] control. Most councillors elected to the council have been Labour or Conservative. The council has had an overall Labour majority since the [[2010 Enfield London Borough Council election|2010 election]], in which Labour won 36 seats and the Conservatives won 27. Save Chase Farm lost both their seats. Labour increased its majority on the council in both subsequent elections in [[2014 Enfield London Borough Council election|2014]] and [[2018 Enfield London Borough Council election|2018]], winning 46 seats with 54.9% of the vote to the Conservatives' seventeen with 35.2% of the vote in the latter.

=== Council term ===
After the 2018 local election, the Labour group voted by 24 votes to 22 to replace their leader Doug Taylor with Nesil Caliskan, who consequently became the leader of the council.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Popular Enfield Labour leader ousted by young candidate|url=https://www.enfieldindependent.co.uk/news/16227177.popular-enfield-labour-leader-ousted/|access-date=2021-09-30|website=Enfield Independent|date=15 May 2018 |language=en}}</ref> She became the borough's first female leader and the youngest council leader in London.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Councillor's pride at being elected Enfield's first female leader|url=https://www.enfieldindependent.co.uk/news/16229186.pride-enfields-first-female-leader/|access-date=2021-09-30|website=Enfield Independent|date=16 May 2018 |language=en}}</ref> In May 2019, her deputy leader Daniel Anderson and four other cabinet members stood down from the council's executive, with Anderson saying he had "been emasculated".<ref>{{Cite web|last=Hill|first=Dave|date=2019-05-13|title=Enfield: Election of new cabinet delights embattled Labour council leader|url=https://www.onlondon.co.uk/enfield-election-of-new-cabinet-delights-embattled-labour-council-leader/|access-date=2021-09-30|website=OnLondon|language=en-GB}}</ref>

In July 2018, Stephanos Ioannou, a Conservative councillor for Southgate ward, was suspended from the party for sharing a 1974 newspaper frontpage covering the Turkish invasion of Cyprus with the headline "Barbarians".<ref name="IouannouDaniels">{{Cite web|title=By-election to be held after Tory councillor resigns|url=https://www.enfieldindependent.co.uk/news/16904137.enfield-tory-councillor-resigns/|access-date=2021-09-30|website=Enfield Independent|date=26 September 2018 |language=en}}</ref> In September 2018, William Coleshill, a Conservative councillor for Bush Hill Park, was suspended from his party after being accused of making racist comments.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Tories suspend councillor accused of making racist comments|url=https://www.enfieldindependent.co.uk/news/16898990.enfield-councillor-suspended-racist-remarks/|access-date=2021-09-30|website=Enfield Independent|date=24 September 2018 |language=en}}</ref> Later the same month, another Conservative councillor for Bush Hill Park, Jon Daniels, resigned citing his work and family commitments.<ref name="IouannouDaniels">{{Cite web|title=By-election to be held after Tory councillor resigns|url=https://www.enfieldindependent.co.uk/news/16904137.enfield-tory-councillor-resigns/|access-date=2021-09-30|website=Enfield Independent|date=26 September 2018 |language=en}}</ref> A by-election to replace him was held in November 2018, which was won by the Conservative candidate, the small business owner James Hockney.<ref>{{Cite web|last=Dispatch|first=Enfield|date=2018-11-23|title=Conservatives triumph in Bush Hill Park by-election|url=https://enfielddispatch.co.uk/conservatives-triumph-in-bush-hill-park-by-election/|access-date=2021-09-30|website=Enfield Dispatch|language=en-GB}}</ref> The Labour councillor Ayfer Orhan was suspended from her party in March 2019 after she shared a tweet claiming that Israel was supporting the [[Islamic State]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Reporter |first=Jewish News |title=Ex-Labour councillor Ayfer Orhan standing for Lib Dems in local election |url=https://www.jewishnews.co.uk/ex-labour-councillor-ayfer-orhan-standing-for-lib-dems-in-local-election/ |access-date=2022-03-23 |website=www.jewishnews.co.uk |date=23 March 2022 |language=en-US}}</ref>

In 2019, Caliskan was found to have broken the council code of conduct after the conduct committee found that her suspension of a cabinet member without meeting her first amounted to bullying, a finding she unsuccessfully appealed.<ref>{{Cite web|last=Dispatch|first=Enfield|date=2019-09-05|title=Council leader loses appeal over bullying case|url=https://enfielddispatch.co.uk/council-leader-loses-appeal-over-bullying-case/|access-date=2021-09-30|website=Enfield Dispatch|language=en-GB}}</ref> In March 2020, Anderson was found to have broken the council code of conduct after complaints from council officers that his behaviour was "aggressive and threatening" and "amounted to bullying".<ref>{{Cite web|last=Dispatch|first=Enfield|date=2020-03-10|title=Bullying claims against former council deputy|url=https://enfielddispatch.co.uk/bullying-claims-against-former-council-deputy/|access-date=2021-09-30|website=Enfield Dispatch|language=en-GB}}</ref> He was subsequently suspended from the Labour Party.<ref name="Anderson">{{Cite web|last=Dispatch|first=Enfield|date=2020-08-05|title=Third councillor quits Labour|url=https://enfielddispatch.co.uk/third-councillor-quits-labour/|access-date=2021-09-30|website=Enfield Dispatch|language=en-GB}}</ref> In July 2020, the Labour councillor Chris Bond died. He had been a councillor in Enfield for more than 34 years.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Tributes paid to long-serving councillor who died last week|url=https://www.enfieldindependent.co.uk/news/18594314.tributes-following-death-enfield-councillor-chris-bond/|access-date=2021-09-30|website=Enfield Independent|date=20 July 2020 |language=en}}</ref> Due to the [[COVID-19 pandemic]], a by-election to replace him could not be held until May 2021. 

In 2020, two Labour councillors who had supported Taylor over Caliskan, Derek Levy and Dinah Barry, left the Labour Party to form a new group on the council called Community First, saying that "the leadership of Enfield Labour group had effectively frozen them out of discussions on policy".<ref>{{Cite web|last=Dispatch|first=Enfield|date=2020-07-30|title='Why we quit Labour'|url=https://enfielddispatch.co.uk/why-we-quit-labour/|access-date=2021-09-30|website=Enfield Dispatch|language=en-GB}}</ref> Anderson joined them in August, also criticising Caliskan.<ref name="Anderson"/> A fourth Labour councillor, Dino Lemonides, joined Community First less than a week later calling the Labour group "authoritarian".<ref>{{Cite web|last=Dispatch|first=Enfield|date=2020-08-10|title=Fourth councillor quits Labour|url=https://enfielddispatch.co.uk/fourth-councillor-quits-labour/|access-date=2021-09-30|website=Enfield Dispatch|language=en-GB}}</ref> In December 2020, Vicki Pite, a Labour councillor for Chase ward resigned from the council while remaining a Labour member.<ref>{{Cite web|last=Dispatch|first=Enfield|date=2020-12-10|title=Labour councillor resigns|url=https://enfielddispatch.co.uk/labour-councillor-resigns/|access-date=2021-09-30|website=Enfield Dispatch|language=en-GB}}</ref> In March 2021, one Labour councillor, Anne Brown, defected to Community First, and another, Bernadette Lappage, resigned from the council.<ref>{{Cite web|last=Dispatch|first=Enfield|date=2021-03-02|title=Labour councillor defects, another quits|url=https://enfielddispatch.co.uk/labour-councillor-defects-another-quits/|access-date=2021-09-30|website=Enfield Dispatch|language=en-GB}}</ref> By-elections to replace Bond, Pite and Lappage were all held on 5 May 2021 alongside the [[2021 London mayoral election]] and [[2021 London Assembly election|London Assembly election]]. Bond's seat was won by the Labour candidate, Ayten Guzel.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Southbury councillor says she will work hard to continue predecessor's legacy|url=https://www.enfieldindependent.co.uk/news/19292095.enfield-labour-holds-southbury-seat-large-majority/|access-date=2021-09-30|website=Enfield Independent|date=10 May 2021 |language=en}}</ref> Pite's seat was gained by the Conservative candidate Andrew Thorp, who had campaigned to protect Whitewebbs golf course.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Tories win Enfield Council Chase ward by-election|url=https://www.enfieldindependent.co.uk/news/19289018.conservatives-win-enfield-council-chase-ward-by-election/|access-date=2021-09-30|website=Enfield Independent|date=8 May 2021 |language=en}}</ref> Lappage's seat was won by the Labour candidate Chinelo Anyanwu.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Labour holds Jubilee seat but with reduced vote share|url=https://www.enfieldindependent.co.uk/news/19292155.enfield-labour-holds-jubilee-seat-vote-share/|access-date=2021-09-30|website=Enfield Independent|date=10 May 2021 |language=en}}</ref>

Later in May 2021, a Labour councillor, Charith Gunawardena, defected to the [[Green Party of England and Wales|Green Party]] and joined the Community First group on the council.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Councillor quits Enfield Labour to join Green Party|url=https://www.enfieldindependent.co.uk/news/19310429.councillor-quits-enfield-labour-join-green-party/|access-date=2021-09-30|website=Enfield Independent|date=18 May 2021 |language=en}}</ref> Days later, Orhan resigned from the Labour Party to join Community First shortly before an unsuccessful vote of no confidence in the council's administration.<ref>{{Cite web|last=Dispatch|first=Enfield|date=2021-05-21|title=Labour group defeats 'no confidence' motion against council|url=https://enfielddispatch.co.uk/labour-group-defeats-no-confidence-motion-against-council/|access-date=2021-09-30|website=Enfield Dispatch|language=en-GB}}</ref> She had taken the Labour Party to court over the length of time it had taken to investigate allegations of antisemitism against her.<ref>{{Cite web|last=Dispatch|first=Enfield|date=2021-05-25|title=Ninth councillor to leave Labour group explains why she quit|url=https://enfielddispatch.co.uk/ninth-councillor-to-leave-labour-group-explains-why-she-quit/|access-date=2021-09-30|website=Enfield Dispatch|language=en-GB}}</ref> Coleshill, who had continued to sit as an independent councillor after being suspended from the Conservative Party, was forced to stand down from the council in June 2021 after failing to attend council meetings for six months.<ref>{{Cite web|last=Dispatch|first=Enfield|date=2021-06-18|title=By-election called after independent kicked off council|url=https://enfielddispatch.co.uk/by-election-called-after-independent-kicked-off-council/|access-date=2021-09-30|website=Enfield Dispatch|language=en-GB}}</ref> A by-election to replace him was held in July 2021, which was won by the Conservative candidate Peter Fallart.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Conservatives win Enfield Council Bush Hill Park by-election|url=https://www.enfieldindependent.co.uk/news/19415919.conservatives-win-enfield-council-bush-hill-park-by-election/|access-date=2021-09-30|website=Enfield Independent|date=2 July 2021 |language=en}}</ref> In September 2021, Brown joined the Green Party while remaining a member of Community First.<ref>{{Cite web|last=Dispatch|first=Enfield|date=2021-09-23|title=Second Enfield councillor joins Green Party|url=https://enfielddispatch.co.uk/second-enfield-councillor-joins-green-party/|access-date=2021-09-30|website=Enfield Dispatch|language=en-GB}}</ref> In November 2021, Orhan joined the Liberal Democrats while remaining a member of Community First.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|last=Dispatch|first=Enfield|date=2021-11-17|title=Ex-Labour councillor joins Lib Dems|url=https://enfielddispatch.co.uk/ex-labour-councillor-joins-lib-dems/|access-date=2022-02-15|website=Enfield Dispatch|language=en-GB}}</ref>

Along with most other London boroughs, Enfield was subject to a boundary review ahead of the 2022 election. The [[Local Government Boundary Commission for England]] concluded that the council should have 63 seats, the same as previously, and produced new election boundaries following a period of consultation. The council will have thirteen three-councillor wards and twelve two-councillor wards.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Local Government Boundary Commission for England Consultation Portal|url=https://consultation.lgbce.org.uk/node/15478|access-date=2021-09-30|website=consultation.lgbce.org.uk}}</ref>

== Campaign ==
The [[Liberal Democrats (UK)|Liberal Democrats]] announced that they would campaign jointly with some independent candidates in an alliance called "Together for Enfield".<ref name=":0" />

== Electoral process ==
Enfield, like other London borough councils, elects all of its councillors at once every four years. The previous election took place in 2018. The election took place by multi-member [[first-past-the-post voting]], with each ward being represented by two or three councillors. Electors had as many votes as there are councillors to be elected in their ward, with the top two or three being elected.

All [[Elections in the United Kingdom#Registration procedure|registered electors]] ([[British citizen|British]], [[Irish citizen|Irish]], [[Commonwealth citizen|Commonwealth]] and [[European Union]] citizens) living in London aged 18 or were entitled to vote in the election. People who lived at two addresses in different councils, such as university students with different term-time and holiday addresses, were entitled to be registered for and vote in elections in both local authorities.<ref name=":1">{{Cite web|title=How the elections work {{!}} London Councils|url=https://www.londoncouncils.gov.uk/who-runs-london/london-elections/how-elections-work|access-date=2021-09-14|website=www.londoncouncils.gov.uk}}</ref> Voting in-person at polling stations took place from 7:00 to 22:00 on election day, and voters were able to apply for postal votes or proxy votes in advance of the election.<ref name=":1" />
